desc:
The integer array nums is sorted in non-decreasing order. A chain is a group of values of the form v, v+1, v+2, ..., v+len-1 (each value one more than the previous) taken from nums.

Decide whether every element of nums can be assigned to exactly one chain so that every chain has at least minLen elements. Return true if this is possible, otherwise false.

nums = [1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5], minLen = 3          -> true   ([1,2,3] and [3,4,5])
nums = [1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5], minLen = 3    -> true   ([1,2,3,4,5] and [3,4,5])
nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5], minLen = 3          -> false
hints: The smallest remaining value must start a chain. The real question is, when a value can both extend a chain and start a new one, which is better?
Extending a chain that is already waiting for exactly this value is never worse than starting a new chain with it (merge the two chains in any solution that does otherwise).

Go through the distinct values in order, keeping the number of chains ending at the previous value, grouped by their start value. If the current value occurs more often than there are chains, the surplus starts new chains. If it occurs less often, the chains that must stop are the oldest (longest) ones; check each has length at least minLen.
editorial: Process the distinct values in increasing order and keep a queue of groups (start value, how many chains) for the chains that end at the previous value. Let p be the number of such chains and c the count of the current value x (if x is not the previous value plus one, every open chain must stop first).

If c ≥ p, all p chains are extended by x (stopping a chain just to start another at the same place could be merged back into one longer chain) and the c - p surplus copies start new chains. If c < p, exactly p - c chains must stop here, and we stop those that started earliest, because they are the longest and the others still need time to reach minLen. A stopped group with length x - start < minLen means false. At the very end all open chains are checked in the same way.
Each value is handled once and queue groups are popped at most once, so the running time is linear after counting.
